fixes.summary: Connecticut’s interest ran in fractions of a cent and the whole owed was rounded, so the interest took a cent of the penalty’s rounding: the bill on $585.33 was $649.72, its interest $5.86, where 1% of $585.33 is $5.85 (Conn. Gen. Stat. 12-735). Each month’s interest is to the cent now (SLATE’s reading of “per month”), so it no longer hangs on how often the balance was brought up to date. What moved: the bill $649.72 → $649.71; the lien $655.57 → $655.56; on 25 June $661.42 → $661.41, the $100 splitting $17.56/$23.91 → $17.55/$23.92; the plan’s 1 May interest $4.87 → $4.88; three months read at once from the bill $17.57 → $17.55. Applies to every monthly-simple authority in STATE_TAX: Connecticut, Georgia, Hawaii, Oklahoma, and the Philadelphia, Columbus and Portland city taxes. No other test moved.

fixes.summary: A state’s penalty, interest and collection ran from the federal return’s due date, which for a 1040-NR without wages is 15 June. Connecticut’s return is due “on or before the fifteenth day of the fourth month” (Conn. Gen. Stat. 12-719(a), codes.findlaw.com, read 2026-10-15), and DRS’s Nonresident and Part-Year Resident Tax Information page (portal.ct.gov, read 2026-10-15) gives 15 April with no other date for a nonresident alien; DRS moves it past Emancipation Day as the IRS does (Form CT-1040NR/PY instructions for 2017: due 17 April 2018). stateDueOf takes the resident’s date for a 1040-NR; every state-side reader goes through it (statetax.ts, taxreturn.ts’s state lines, Papers’ state rows). The other states and cities in STATE_TAX take the same date as SLATE’s reading, unread state by state; no played life files in them.

recheck.problem: The bill’s $649.72 against its parts ($585.33 + $58.53 + $5.85 = $649.71); the 1 May interest $4.87 against 1% of $487.77 = $4.88.
recheck.done: A defect, fixed. The engine ran monthly interest in fractions of a cent and rounded the whole, giving the interest what was left. Each month’s 1% is to the cent now (stateAccrual). What moved: $649.72 → $649.71, $655.57 → $655.56, $661.42 → $661.41 (the $100 to $17.55 interest, $23.92 tax), $4.87 → $4.88, and a new assertion that three months read at once from the bill are $17.55, the same as charged month by month (it was $17.57). Rounding each part separately while keeping the unrounded monthly increments was tried first. For Connecticut it was equivalent once each month is to the cent, and it survived every tax test, so it was reverted rather than kept untested. The whole-rounding still applies to the daily-interest states, which no played life reaches.

recheck.problem: stateNextNotice’s fix counted from the federal due date for every state, citing only Connecticut; a 1040-NR with no wages is due 15 June.
recheck.done: A defect, fixed. Conn. Gen. Stat. 12-719(a) and DRS’s nonresident page both give 15 April, with no nonresident-alien exception. stateDueOf gives a 1040-NR’s state side the resident’s date, and every state reader uses it. Tested by ‘a 1040-NR’s 15 June is the IRS’s alone …’, which fails with stateDueOf reverted. It needs TEST SETUP, the due date put at 15 June, because no played life files a wage-free 1040-NR with Connecticut owed: work-study is paid on the clock to every student with need from her first fall, the probe’s six London-born families all had $1,656.00 of it, and a student who withdraws on the first day is off her F-1 and has no return (probed 2026-10-15).
